steps.body: Multiplication undoes division, so every quotient carries its own proof: multiply it by the divisor and the dividend should come back.
steps.narration: Multiplication undoes division, so every quotient carries its own proof: multiply it by the divisor and the dividend should come back.

commonResults.feedback: 842 stranded the carry from the ones column, so the check falls ten short of 852 — the slip is in the check, not the quotient.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add column by column from the ones; when a column reaches 10 or more, trade and carry.
widget.successFeedback: 24,681 + 13,247 = 37,928 — the ones make 8 with a carry that the tens must include.

predict.prompt: You found 852 ÷ 4 = 213. Which product should rebuild 852?
predict.reveal: The quotient times the divisor reconstructs the dividend — that is exactly what division took apart. Multiplying 852 by 4 again gives 3,408 and checks nothing — 852 is the number you started with; only the quotient 213 paired with the divisor rebuilds it.

cml.actionGoal: Split a factor into places, build each piece, and reassemble the whole for g4m check quotient.
invariants: Splitting a factor never changes the product: every piece of the split multiplies the other factor, and the pieces add back to exactly the same total, which is what makes g4m check quotient decomposable at all.
misconceptions: Adding only some of the partial products, dropping or inventing a zero when factors carry tens, or letting a remainder reach or exceed the divisor.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one partial product were left out, exactly how much of the total would go missing?
